hypothesis: On a Xeon Gold 6254 beside an Arc Pro B60 (Vulkan dense chain, every routed expert in the tier's host pool), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8's hybrid decode steps compute the host pool's FP8 pairs on the CPU through dev_dequant: an ldexpf and an integer division per weight, then a scalar sum; 41 ms a layer step, about 2 s a token with the GPU idle 95% of the time. Decoding the codes through binary16 (F16C) or a table with AVX2, each 128-column group's scale applied once, computes the same pairs about 30x faster: decode several times faster, greedy answers identical.
model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (the release's FP8 e4m3 experts, 128x128 block scales; 185.5 GB), at /models/qwen38-flash-next (config.json sha256 99c11efba4012d0f760f4e4831a8d6cafd845044e21d0aa9e6d9e70a15a90a8d)
command: Build, both trees: docker run --rm -v <tree>:/src -w /src colibri-builder:xe2 nice -n 19 make -C c colibri qwen36 qwen38 VK=1 ARCH=x86-64-v3 (0 warnings); the binaries, c/*.py, c/tools and c/shaders over the same runtime image (Ubuntu 26.04, Mesa 26.2.6). Engine: docker compose up -d of a compose file with coli serve --model /models/qwen38-flash-next --cap 64, COLI_ENGINE=/app/qwen38, COLI_VULKAN=1, only GPU 1's render node mapped, cpuset 16-31, OMP_NUM_THREADS=16, COLI_USAGE= the shipped c/profiles/qwen38-flash-next.coli_usage with USAGE_SAVE=0, and an override with the arm's image and variables. Measured with colibench, a local benchmark harness (not part of this repository): python3 colibench.py run --profile light --micro off --repetitions 3 --warmups 1 --workloads decode_short,prefill_short,prefill_long --timeout 1800, COLIBENCH_REASONING_EFFORT=none (streamed OpenAI API requests, temperature 0); answers: experiments/outputs_check.py.
